question_part: Compares motorist versus cyclist deaths as a proportion of the combined reported deaths for these two road-user types in each year.
metric: For each year, each type's share of the combined motorist and cyclist deaths reported in that year.
denominator: The same year's reported motorist deaths plus reported cyclist deaths; does not include pedestrian deaths or other crash deaths.
population: All police-reported NYC motor vehicle crashes dated in calendar years 2013 through 2025; count the reported motorist/cyclist deaths on each crash row, then compare the two types within year.
grouping: Calendar year and road-user type (motorist, cyclist), expressed as a share of the two-type annual total.

initial_data_check.facts: The requested years each have crash rows; crash_date is missing on 0 rows in the file; each year has observed dates from January 1 through December 31; the two killed-person columns each have 0 missing values in the target population and in every year.
initial_data_check.meaning_and_decisions: No target-year crash rows or annual death entries are excluded for missingness. Keep all target-year rows and disclose that values are reported fatality counts. Full-year endpoints support treating each requested calendar year as covered, although endpoints alone do not establish that every date is represented. No columns in this plan are string-grouped, so empty/unknown category labels and default category values do not apply.

limitations: Shares describe only the split between reported motorist and cyclist deaths, excluding pedestrians and any other road-user deaths. They are composition shares, not per-capita, per-trip, or per-crash risk; full-year endpoints do not prove daily completeness or validate non-NULL death values.
